headline: AI virtual patients speed up colposcopy reasoning, but not hands-on skill
intro: In a randomised trial, residents trained with an AI virtual-patient platform reasoned and communicated better after a month, but their operative skill was no different.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced colposcopy training improves diagnostic reasoning and communication competencies: A randomized controlled study
items.source: Journal of Gynecology Obstetrics and Human Reproduction
items.summary: In a randomised, assessor-blinded, wait-list trial, 60 PGY-2 and PGY-3 obstetrics and gynecology residents at two affiliated teaching hospitals added an AI virtual-patient platform to their usual colposcopy teaching either straight away or a month later. At one month the AI group scored higher on case analysis (78.57 vs 71.03, a mean difference of 7.54), diagnostic justification and communication, but operative competence did not differ (p = 0.113), and both groups were proficient by three months. It was a small, single-specialty trial with short follow-up, scored on OSCEs rather than patient care.
items.why_it_matters: AI virtual patients look like a way to speed up practice in diagnostic reasoning and communication. Programs should not assume that talking a case through with an AI builds hands-on procedural skill.
